questions.text:
Which of the following is/are correct inorder traversal sequence(s) of binary search tree(s)?
I. 3, 5, 7, 8, 15, 19, 25
II. 5, 8, 9, 12, 10, 15, 25
III. 2, 7, 10, 8, 14, 16, 20
IV. 4, 6, 7, 9 18, 20, 25
questions.solution:
In-order traversal of a BST is always sorted.

- I: sorted [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] valid
- II: 12 before 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] invalid
- III: 10 before 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] invalid
- IV: sorted [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] valid

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text: The height of a tree is the length of the longest root-to-leaf path in it. The maximum and minimum number of nodes in a binary tree of height 5 are
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Maximum: complete tree with levels 0 to 5 = [latex]2^6-1=63[/latex] nodes
- Minimum: a single path of 5 edges = 6 nodes

Answer: 63 and 6

questions.text: How many different trees are there with four nodes A,B,C and D?
questions.solution:
Taking trees as rooted and ordered (the order of children matters), the number of shapes with 4 nodes is the Catalan number [latex]C_3=5[/latex].

Labelling the nodes with A, B, C, D in 4! = 24 ways: 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 24 = 120.

Answer: 120

questions.text: Consider a 13 element hash table for which f(key)=key mod 13 is used with integer keys. Assuming linear probing is used for collision resolution, at which location would the key 103 be inserted, if the keys 661, 182, 24 and 103 are inserted in that order?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 661 mod 13 = 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] slot 11
- 182 mod 13 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] slot 0
- 24 mod 13 = 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] taken, go to 12
- 103 mod 13 = 12 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] taken, 0 taken, 1 free [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] slot 1

Answer: 1

questions.text: Consider a single linked list where F and L are pointers to the first and last elements respectively of the linked list. The time for performing which of the given operations depends on the length of the linked list?
questions.solution:
To delete the last node we must set its predecessor's next to NULL. Finding the predecessor needs a traversal from F, so it is O(n).

Deleting/swapping at the front, and adding after L, take O(1).

Answer: Delete the last element of the list
